articles.title: Nader bate a Mariano García en el duelo de campeones del mundo de Berango
articles.standfirst: En la prueba femenina, la keniana Mirriam Cherot, bronce en el reciente Campeonato del Mundo de la milla, superó en un apretadísimo sprint final a la portuguesa Salomé Afonso
articles.summary: En la prueba femenina, la keniana Mirriam Cherot, bronce en el reciente Campeonato del Mundo de la milla, superó en un apretadísimo sprint final a la portuguesa Salomé Afonso
articles.body: El portugués Isaac Nader fue el ganador de la XXXVIII Milla Internacional de Berango tras superar al murciano Mariano García en el gran duelo entre campeones del mundo de 1.500 metros que ha acaparado el interés de la prueba vizcaína. Nader, oro en el Mundial de Tokio 2025, logró su sexta victoria consecutiva en el circuito de Gobelalde tras superar con autoridad en el sprint final a García, campeón mundial en pista cubierta en Torun (Polonia), en marzo, después de superar al propio corredor luso. La lluvia que empezó a caer unos minutos antes de comenzar las carreras principales no deslució una prueba disputada a buen ritmo en la que Pablo Sánchez-Valladares encabezó el pelotón con Nader a su estela y García, algo más apurado, por detrás. Fue en el último giro cuando el portugués tomó definitivamente el mando para imponer un ritmo imposible de seguir para sus rivales a pesar del esfuerzo final de García, segundo, y del granadino Nacho Fonte, que acabó en tercera posición. Cuarto fue el francés Louis Gilavert. En la carrera femenina, disputada a continuación bajo un fuerte aguacero, la keniana Mirriam Cherot, bronce en el reciente Campeonato del Mundo de la Milla, superó en un apretadísimo sprint final a la portuguesa Salomé Afonso, que no pudo lograr su cuarto triunfo en Berango. Completó el podio la barcelonesa Marta Mitjans.

articles.title: Egoitz se queda a un paso del podio mundial de Vert
articles.standfirst: El campeón mundial de Park termina cuarto en Asunción con 232,33 puntos antes de afrontar la defensa de su corona en su especialidad
articles.summary: El campeón mundial de Park termina cuarto en Asunción con 232,33 puntos antes de afrontar la defensa de su corona en su especialidad
articles.body: Egoitz Bijueska ya está entre los mejores del mundo también en Vert. El skater español ha terminado cuarto en la final del Mundial de Asunción con 232,33 puntos, rozando un podio internacional que hasta hace muy poco parecía reservado a especialistas de la gran rampa. El oro fue para el estadounidense JD Sanchez, que cerró la competición con 274,46 puntos. El brasileño Gui Khury se proclamó subcampeón con 265,25 y Hudson Walker completó el podio con 244,39. Egoitz se quedó a solo 12,06 puntos del bronce. El resultado adquiere otra dimensión cuando se observa la especialidad principal del bilbaíno. Bijueska es el vigente campeón mundial de Park y uno de los grandes talentos internacionales de la modalidad. Sin embargo, durante esta temporada ha comenzado a demostrar que su capacidad para volar por encima del coping puede trasladarse también al Vert. En junio fue quinto en los X Games de Sacramento y posteriormente terminó cuarto en Tony Hawk's Vert Alert, uno de los eventos de referencia de la disciplina. En Paraguay ha llevado esa progresión hasta un Campeonato del Mundo. La final reunió además a una generación extraordinaria. Gui Khury, uno de los grandes referentes mundiales del Vert, tuvo que conformarse con la plata ante JD Sanchez, mientras Walker cerró las posiciones de medalla. Tras Egoitz terminaron el japonés Ruku Inui, CJ Hawker, Ao Nishikawa y Magnus Magiar. Para el español, sin embargo, Paraguay todavía está lejos de terminar. El próximo desafío será precisamente el más importante. Bijueska deberá cambiar el Vert por el bowl para disputar el Mundial de Park, la disciplina en la que llega como vigente campeón después del título conquistado esta temporada en São Paulo. Lo hará con una certeza nueva. Egoitz llegó a Asunción como campeón mundial de Park y acaba de quedarse a un solo puesto de subir al podio mundial de Vert. Con 15 años, el español ya no parece dispuesto a elegir entre las dos paredes.

articles.title: EXCLUSIVE | Asian Games gold done, Neeru Dhanda eyes Olympic shotgun medal to end wait since Rajyavardhan Rathore’s 2004 silver
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Days before leaving for the Asian Games 2026, Neeru Dhanda was hospitalised with viral fever.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Days before leaving for the Asian Games 2026, Neeru Dhanda was hospitalised with viral fever. She had barely any time to recover before boarding the flight to Japan. There was no proper recovery period. Just medicines, ORS, and a dream of winning a medal at the Asian Games.When she reached Aichi-Nagoya and entered her hotel room, Neeru picked up her gun and told herself three words: "Nerru, tu training pe hai (Neeru, you are in training."It was a message she wanted to give her own mind - a way of staying focused and refusing to think about the illness.With water bottles, ORS and medicines by her side, Neeru kept her dream alive. The trap shooter, who had won gold at the ISSF World Cup in Lonato earlier this year, eventually stepped onto the range, loaded her ammunition and shot her way to glory.She finished the Asian Games with three medals - two golds and a silver - emerging as one of India's standout performers.From illness to three medalsNeeru first won gold in the women's individual trap event. She then teamed up with Manisha Keer and Aashima Ahlawat to win silver in the women's trap team event. On the penultimate day of the shooting competition, she partnered Kynan Chenai to win gold in the trap mixed team event.But behind the three medals was a battle that began even before she reached the shooting range.“I didn't let my mind receive the message that I was sick or unwell. I didn't want to let myself think that I was sick. Whenever I felt down or weak, I used to tell myself loudly, ‘Neeru, tu training pe hai abhi.’ This is what kept me motivated throughout the Asian Games,” Neeru told TimesofIndia.com in an exclusive interview.“Honestly, I felt very weak because there was no recovery period after the hospitalisation. I thought about skipping the Games, but no, I am very stubborn. I wanted to do something different. Very few people get this opportunity. I was lucky that I got it, and I am happy that I delivered,” she said.A medal dedicated to Raja Randhir SinghNeeru dedicated her three-medal haul to late Raja Randhir Singh, India's first Asian Games shooting gold medallist, who passed away aged 79 in May. Randhir, a five-time Olympian, had won India's first Asian Games shooting gold in 1978.Neeru had met him a few times and remembered the encouragement he gave her.“I dedicate these medals to late Raja Randhir Singh. He was a lovely soul. I got to meet him a couple of times. Whenever he met me, he blessed me. He always said, ‘Beta, be brave. You are a shooter, you need to be brave. Shoot with bravery, you will get the result.’ Those words helped me a lot in Aichi-Nagoya,” Neeru said."I also want to dedicate to my federation, SAI, SAI Bhopal, Bhopa Shooting Academy where I train, my coaches, and everyone who has been with me throughout this journey," she said.Mission Olympics beginsThe World Cup is done. The Asian Games are done. Now, Neeru has set her sights on the Los Angeles Olympics. Her immediate target is the World Championship in Doha, which will offer a quota opportunity for the 2028 Olympics.“The moment I leave Japan, my target will shift towards the World Championship in Doha. That is a quota competition for the Los Angeles Olympics, so I will focus on that. That is my ultimate goal. Olympics mein medal jeetna hai,” she said.India have won several Olympic medals in shooting, but the shotgun disciplines have produced only one Olympic medal for the country - Rajyavardhan Singh Rathore's silver in men's double trap at the 2004 Athens Olympics.After her performances in Aichi-Nagoya, Neeru will be one of the Indian shooters attracting attention ahead of the Los Angeles Games.‘Golden girl’? Neeru loves itNeeru has also earned the nickname ‘golden girl’ after her recent run of success. Asked about the title, she laughed.“Golden girl title... I just love it. I love this title. I hope it continues to be like this always. It was possible because of the hard work I have put in day and night,” she said.For Neeru, the key has been constantly looking back at her own performances and learning from her mistakes.“Introspection has always helped me. Whenever I do something wrong or make mistakes, I ask myself, ‘Where did I go wrong?’ I get that answer. That helps me a lot,” she said.Little time with familyAfter returning home with three medals, Neeru was eager to meet her parents and family and celebrate her success with them.But she had only a few hours. Neeru was at her home in Sangatpura village in Jind, speaking to her mother, when she received a call that gave her another reason to return to Japan.Former India shooter and deputy chef de mission Anjali Bhagwat told her that she had been selected as India's women's flag bearer for the closing ceremony of the Asian Games 2026. Within hours, Neeru packed her bags and headed back to the airport.“I got a call from Anjali Bhagwat ma'am. She asked me to be the flag bearer at the closing ceremony. It's a big honour for me. I didn't want to let it go,” Neeru told TimesofIndia.com.Her parents were delighted by the news. “My parents are so happy. When I gave them the news about the closing ceremony, my mother said, ‘Ja beta, mauka nahi milta ye kisi ko. Aaja, phir se khushi manayenge,’” Neeru said.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Kiptoo bate un récord del mundo en el Medio Maratón de San Sebastián Rural Kutxa
articles.standfirst: El keniano ha corrido en 1h03:57, destrozando la anterior plusmarca mundial M50 (1h06:17).
articles.summary: El keniano ha corrido en 1h03:57, destrozando la anterior plusmarca mundial M50 (1h06:17).
articles.body: Se buscaba un récord mundial en Donostia y se ha logrado. Mark Kosgey Kiptoo, un hombre que llegó a ser campeón africano en pista y capitán de la poderosa selección keniana de cross, ha mejorado este domingo en la quinta edición del Medio Maratón de San Sebastián Rural Kutxa el mejor registro jamás logrado por un atleta mayor de 50 años en los 21,097 kilómetros. Kiptoo ha corrido en 1h03:57, destrozando la anterior plusmarca mundial M50 (era 1h06:17). El exitoso y veterano atleta, que había llegado a la capital guipuzcoana con ese objetivo entre ceja y ceja antes de retirarse, ha sido el gran protagonista en una carrera con 5.200 inscritos (otro récord) en la que Maitane Melero ha sido la triunfadora femenina, la mujer que se ha llevado la txapela de campeona. La navarra, que llegó a ser finalista en un Europeo en pista y es cinco veces campeona de España absoluta, se ha impuesto con un crono de 1h15:44, dando lustre a un palmarés de la prueba en la que hay otros nombres importantes para el atletismo español como Meritxell Soler, Irene Pelayo o Elena Loyo. Tanto Kiptoo como Melero eran los grandes favoritos y no han defraudado. En la carrera masculina, el local Joseba Díaz ha sido el encargado de marcar el ritmo, cercano a 3:05 durante los primeros kilómetros. Ha tirado hasta pasado el séptimo kilómetro aproximadamente, momento en el que Kiptoo se ha quedado en cabeza con Iraitz Arrospide. El keniano, al ver que tenía más en sus piernas, ha acelerado y se ha marchado al poco de abandonar la liebre. Animado por el siempre fiel público donostiarra, Kiptoo ha cabalgado en solitario hasta la meta. Y ha lucido con orgullo el cartelón del récord mundial máster. Por detrás, Arrospide, en una gran carrera, ha completado los 21,097 kilómetros en 1h04:51. Tercero, de menos a más, ha llegado Youness Assehli (1h07:19). En la carrera femenina, el ritmo inicial lo ha marcado la madrileña María Lázaro. La madrileña, campeona de España de maratón en 2025, ha visto cómo la única mujer capaz de seguirle era Melero. A la altura del octavo kilómetro, Lázaro ha comenzado a ceder y ha sido la navarra la que ha puesto tierra de por medio. Ha disfrutado y se ha hecho con la victoria. Segunda finalmente ha sido la suiza Janice Studler (1h18:19), que ha pasado en los metros finales a Lázaro (1h18:27).

articles.title: Asian Games: Olympic Council of Asia cites 54 world records to declare Aichi-Nagoya Games a success despite chaos
articles.summary: The Olympic Council of Asia (OCA) has defended the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Games as a success, pointing to 54 world records, strong viewership and a
articles.body: The Olympic Council of Asia (OCA) has defended the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Games as a success, pointing to 54 world records, strong viewership and a nearly 20% increase in revenue despite persistent logistical problems that marred the continental sporting showpiece.OCA Director General Husain Al-Musallam said the record-breaking performances demonstrated that athletes had the environment needed to deliver exceptional results during the Games, which concluded on Sunday.A total of 54 world records, 11 junior world records and 89 continental records were set during the competition, providing the OCA with evidence of the event's sporting success despite complaints over accommodation and transportation."This achievement does not come without the best environment," Al-Musallam told reporters at a press conference on the final day of the Games."The athletes cannot perform if they don't have transportation. The athletes cannot perform if they don't have good healthcare. The athletes cannot perform if they don't eat food. Number talks, it's evidence. We are here to present you with the evidence."OCA highlights records, revenue growthAl-Musallam also highlighted the financial sustainability of the Aichi-Nagoya model, arguing that major sporting events did not necessarily require expensive infrastructure projects that could become underused after the competition."We are happy to see that there is no big financial burden in the organising committee, and there is no white elephant staying in Nagoya or any place," he said.The OCA attributed the nearly 20% revenue increase compared with the Hangzhou 2023 Asian Games largely to digital growth and stronger viewership. India's hockey and cricket matches against Pakistan were among the fixtures that attracted large television audiences.Weightlifting was a major contributor to the record-breaking spectacle, with 25 senior world records established in the sport. North Korea led the way with 15 world records, while China also produced a series of outstanding performances.The Games attracted around 17,000 athletes and officials following a surge in late entries, approximately 2,000 more than initially projected.Logistical problems remain a concernThe sporting achievements, however, came against a backdrop of organisational difficulties. Without a dedicated athletes' village, participants were accommodated in hotels, container-style living units and a cruise ship.The unexpected increase in registrations strained accommodation and transport arrangements, prompting complaints about cramped rooms, small beds and unreliable transportation. Organising committee secretary general Satoshi Murate apologised for the problems.OCA officials nevertheless argued that the Games demonstrated the power of sport to bring countries together amid international tensions."When you look to the news, conflict everywhere - in Asia, outside Asia," Al-Musallam said. "Economic problems everywhere. But look at Asia, how united we are in sport."Tayyab Ikram, chairman of the Games Coordination Committee, acknowledged that improvements were necessary."There is no Games without challenges. There are no Games without initial interruptions," Ikram said."In the future, we would like to see more sustainable solutions, more improvement and innovation ... but without compromising on the athletes' conditions."As Doha prepares to host the 2030 Asian Games, the Aichi-Nagoya edition has left organisers with two contrasting legacies: a remarkable collection of sporting records and a reminder that operational efficiency must match athletic ambition.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Learn from these Games and keep moving forward’: Abhinav Bindra’s message to Team India as LA Olympics beckons
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Olympic gold medallist Abhinav Bindra has urged Indian athletes to learn from both the successes and disappointments of the Asian Games 2026,
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Olympic gold medallist Abhinav Bindra has urged Indian athletes to learn from both the successes and disappointments of the Asian Games 2026, calling for stronger high-performance systems and a renewed focus on preparations for the Los Angeles Olympics, which are less than two years away.Congratulating India's athletes and support teams after the country finished fourth in the Aichi-Nagoya Games with 85 medals, Bindra highlighted the years of hard work and sacrifices behind their performances while stressing the need for an honest assessment of the campaign.India finished with 21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze medals, falling short of its record haul of 106 medals at Hangzhou 2023. However, the campaign produced several historic achievements, including gold-medal sweeps in men's and women's cricket, kabaddi and hockey.In a lengthy post on X on Sunday, Bindra thanked athletes, their families, coaches and support staff for their contributions before urging the sporting establishment to turn the lessons from Aichi-Nagoya into meaningful improvements.'Enormous respect to our athletes'"Congratulations to every Indian athlete and to Team India on the Asian Games. A Games campaign is never just the few days we see on television. It is years of early mornings, injuries, doubts, missed occasions and countless hours of work," Bindra wrote."So first and foremost, enormous respect to our athletes and also to their families who live this journey with them and make sacrifices that are rarely seen. To the coaches, support staff, federations, SAI, the Government and everyone working behind the scenes, THANK YOU!"The 2008 Beijing Olympics gold medallist in shooting acknowledged the breakthrough performances in Aichi-Nagoya, particularly those of young athletes who announced themselves on the continental stage. However, he stressed that disappointments must also be examined rather than simply forgotten."There have been some terrific breakthrough performances at these Games. Young athletes have announced themselves, others have stepped up to a new level, and there have been moments that give us a lot to be excited about. There have also been disappointments. That is sport, and every Games will have them. What matters now is how honestly we learn from them," he added.'LA is less than two years away'Bindra called for a more comprehensive approach to athlete development, arguing that high-performance programmes must provide the right expertise throughout an athlete's career rather than stepping in only when medals are within reach."High performance cannot only be about reacting when an athlete is close to a medal. We have to keep building systems that understand the athlete over several years," he wrote.He emphasised the importance of sports science, data-driven decisions, coaching, competition planning, training-load management, recovery and injury prevention, alongside building physical and mental resilience."Most importantly, the right expertise has to reach the athlete at the right stage of their career, not when it is already too late," he said.With the next Summer Olympics approaching, Bindra warned that the preparation window was shrinking and called for immediate action."LA is less than two years away. In Olympic sport, that is not a long time. The athletes who will stand on the podium there are already deep into their preparation today."His message was to celebrate the achievements, acknowledge shortcomings and return to work with renewed determination."Be proud of what has been achieved. Learn from these Games and keep moving forward. Wishing Team India everything good on the road to LA," he concluded.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Town could become Olympic training hub
articles.summary: Plans for a specialist obstacle course at the Whalley Road sports complex are been approved.
articles.body:
A town could become home to a unique training facility for one of the Olympic Games' newest disciplines after plans for a specialist obstacle course were approved.

The facility will be built at Wilsons Playing Fields in Clayton-le-Moors, Lancashire, after Hyndburn Borough Council granted planning permission.

Application documents said the development was intended to support the growing obstacle racing discipline in modern pentathlon and was believed to be "the only training rig of its kind north of Bath in the UK".

The permanent facility will be within the athletics track at the Whalley Road sports complex, operated by Hyndburn Leisure.

According to the Local Democracy Reporting Service , plans show the steel-framed structure will measure about 10.5m (34ft) long, 6.5m (21ft) wide and up to (13ft) 4m high.

It will occupy a 272 sq m compound in the centre of the athletics infield and be surrounded by 2.4m (6.5ft) high anti-climb fencing.

The development reflects a major change in modern pentathlon, with the sport's governing body replacing horse riding with obstacle racing.

The new format has since been approved for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic Games.

Modern pentathlon will now consist of fencing, swimming, obstacle racing and the laser run, which combines running and shooting.

Olympic organisers have described the obstacle element as a head-to-head sprint course inspired by the popularity of Ninja-style challenges.

A council report said the rig would be positioned alongside existing athletics infrastructure, including the pole vault and javelin areas, and would not result in the loss of any sports provision.

The report also noted that goalposts, lighting, fencing and sports equipment already exist across the wider site, reducing the visual impact of the development.

No objections were received from statutory consultees, including Sport England and the council's ecology officers, while nearby residents did not submit any comments.

articles.title: 'It's like water to a thirsty person': Asian Games gold reignites women's hockey at grassroots
articles.summary: KOLKATA: The Indian women’s hockey team’s Asian Games gold medal after a 44-year wait has done more than secure direct qualification for the Olympics.
articles.body: KOLKATA: The Indian women’s hockey team’s Asian Games gold medal after a 44-year wait has done more than secure direct qualification for the Olympics.According to coaches who have nurtured generations of players across the country, the triumph has rekindled belief at the grassroots, and is destined to inspire a new generation of girls to take up the sport while validating decades of hard work in academies and training centres, far from the spotlight.Former India captain Pritam Siwach, who has been working as a coach for more than 25 years in Sonipat, Haryana, believes the impact of the victory extends well beyond the podium.“This victory has given women’s hockey a new lease of life. It is like giving water to a thirsty person. Winning gold after 44 years has ended a long drought and brought renewed energy to the sport,” she said, adding that the success has given women’s hockey the recognition it deserves after years of operating in the shadow of the men’s game.For coaches working at the grassroots level, the medal has become a powerful tool. Dasrath Mahato, the 69-year-old from Khunti in Jharkhand who discovered and mentored Nikki Pradhan, said every major success creates a ripple effect among young athletes.“When children see players returning home with medals, they start to believe they can do the same. It inspires them to work harder and pursue hockey seriously,” Mahato said.The success has also been celebrated by coaches who have worked in some of the country’s leading hockey centres. Madhya Pradesh Hockey Academy coach Vandana says achievements at the elite level invariably strengthen the grassroots ecosystem.“When a sport performs well at the top level, it benefits the grassroots. We are already seeing more academies and leagues being established for women, and success like this will only accelerate that growth,” said Vandana, who trained the likes of Sushila Chanu and Bichu Devi Kharibam.Former India goalkeeper and coach Edgar Mascarenhas, who worked extensively in Odisha, described the achievement as one of the biggest milestones in the history of Indian women’s hockey.“I watched every match and what impressed me most was their fighting spirit. Even in difficult situations, they never gave up,” said Mascarenhas.The direct Olympic qualification has also been highlighted as one of the competition’s biggest outcomes. Coaches unanimously agreed that avoiding the pressure of an additional qualification campaign allows the team to focus entirely on preparation for the Games.“This may actually be even more important than the gold medal itself,” said Siwach. “Now the players know they are going to the Olympics and can devote all their energy towards preparing for that challenge.”The impact has been felt in regions that have emerged as strong contributors to Indian women’s hockey. In Mizoram, where coach Miss Btei helped nurture internationals Lalremsiami and Lalthantluangi, interest in the sport continues to grow among young children.“The success of players from our state will encourage more youngsters to take up hockey. Children see what Lalremsiami has achieved and begin to believe they can follow the same path,” she said.According to Btei, players as young as nine or ten years old, are now entering the development pathway with the latest generation already benefiting from the visibility created by the national team’s success.For former India international and coach Ajit Lakra, the gold medal represents proof that India’s grassroots structures are delivering results.“These players came through the grassroots system and delivered a gold-medal performance that resonated across Asia. It shows young athletes that there is a pathway from the grassroots level to the international stage,” said Lakra, who coached Rutuja Dadaso Pisal.While they welcomed the growing number of opportunities for women, the coaches stressed the importance of greater investment in infrastructure, academies and player development programmes to sustain the momentum.Yet the overriding sentiment remains one of optimism. Whether in hockey strongholds like Jharkhand and Odisha, established academies in Madhya Pradesh or emerging centres like Mizoram, coaches see the medal as a catalyst for growth.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: La convocatoria de elecciones 'golpea' el calendario atlético del 29 de noviembre
articles.standfirst: El medio maratón de Sevilla es el que más corredores inscritos tiene esa jornada, en la que también están previstas la Allianz Jean Bouin o el maratón Elche-Alicante
articles.summary: El medio maratón de Sevilla es la que más corredores inscritos esa jornada, en la que también estaban previstas la Allianz Jean Bouin o el medio maratón de Córdoba
articles.body: La convocatoria de elecciones anticipadas anunciada por el presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, para el próximo 29 de noviembre ha golpeado el calendario atlético de pruebas en ruta previsto para esa jornada dominical. La carrera con más inscritos prevista para ese día es el medio maratón de Sevilla, en el que se pusieron a disposición 20.000 dorsales. La prueba tiene su salida y meta en el Paseo de las Delicias. La organización ya ha hecho público que se encuentra manteniendo "reuniones con las autoridades competentes por el anuncio de elecciones generales para el 29 de noviembre. Os mantendremos informados sobre cualquier novedad". La mayoría de estas carreras tienen fijado su horario de inicio a las 9.00 de la mañana, justo el momento en el que se produce la apertura de los colegios electorales. Los 21,097 kilómetros de la capital hispalense no son la única prueba en ruta prevista para el 29 de noviembre. También el calendario recoge la celebración de la 103 edición de la Allianz Jean Bouin, en Barcelona, con distancias de 10 kilómetros y 5 kilómetros. Se trata de una prueba que también congrega a más de 15.000 corredores entre todas las distancias. Se pueden ver afectadas el medio maratón de Córdoba o la carrera Desde Santurce a Bilbao, así como la segunda edición del maratón Elche-Alicante. Esta carrera se encuentra también ya en conversaciones con los ayuntamientos y las Fuerzas de Seguridad para valorar alternativas.

articles.title: Alex Ovechkin: NHL legend will retire at end of season with Washington Capitals
articles.summary: National Hockey League all-time leading goalscorer Alex Ovechkin says he will retire at the end of the season.
articles.body:
National Hockey League all-time leading goalscorer Alex Ovechkin says he will retire at the end of the season.

The 41-year-old Russian, who plays for the Washington Capitals, claimed the record in April 2025 when he scored his 895th career goal to surpass the legendary Wayne Gretzky's NHL regular season tally.

Canadian Hall of Famer Gretzky held the record for 31 years having previously overtaken compatriot Gordie Howe in 1994.

Ovechkin said in a statement that he "loves this game so much" but knew that in his "heart it's the right decision".

"It was important for me to make this announcement before our first home game, so I have the chance to thank all the people around the game," Ovechkin said.

"Everyone who has been so important to me and my family and helped me through good times and tough losses.

"I wouldn't have been able to achieve everything I have in my life without them."

Ovechkin has 1,688 career points (929 goals, 759 assists) in 1,575 games for the Capitals, the 10th-most points in NHL history.

He's 11 goals away from passing Gretzky for most total goals (regular season and play-offs combined) in NHL history and four assists away from passing Nicklas Backstrom for the franchise career assists record (762).

Ovechkin will play his first Western Conference home game of the new season on Wednesday when the Pittsburgh Penguins are the visitors to the Capital One Arena.

"I am excited about this season with my team-mates, and we will do everything we can to make this year special," he added.

"I am going to enjoy every moment with my family, my boys, our fans and everyone who has been part of my hockey career."

Ovechkin has been a mainstay for the Washington Capitals since his NHL debut in October 2005.

He was selected first overall by the Capitals in the 2004 NHL Draft after establishing himself as one of the brightest young talents in Russian hockey.

He moved to North America from Dynamo Moscow at the age of 20 and scored twice on his NHL debut against the Columbus Blue Jackets.

Ovechkin helped the Capitals to their only Stanley Cup victory in 2017-18 and has scored at least 40 goals in 14 of his 21 NHL seasons, an NHL record.

Known for his passionate celebrations and relaxed attitude towards the strict diets expected in the modern game, his face is plastered across the league's marketing material.

articles.title: María Pérez, entre las 10 nominadas a atleta del año por World Athletics
articles.standfirst: La española, campeona de Europa de medio maratón marcha, aspira al galardón junto a atletas como Audrey Werro, Tigst Assefa o Chase Jackson, entre otras
articles.summary: La española, campeona de Europa de medio maratón marcha, aspira al galardón junto a atletas como Audrey Werro, Tigst Assefa o Chase Jackson, entre otras
articles.body: La española María Pérez es una de las 10 nominadas a atleta del año por World Athletics, un premio que en 2025 obtuvo Sydney McLaughlin, en categoría femenina. María Pérez se proclamó este año campeona de Europa de medio maratón marcha, el estreno continental de la distancia, con un tiempo de 1.30.06, que se convirtió también en el primer registro en formalizarse como récord del mundo de la disciplina. Junto a ella, están nominadas la dominicana Marileidy Paulino, la etíope Tigst Assefa, las estadounidenses Chase Jackson, Melissa Jefferson-Wooden y Masai Russell, la keniana Agnes Ngetich, la canadiense Camryn Rogers, la suiza Audrey Werro y la china Yan Ziyi. En categoría masculina, el plusmarquista mundial de pértiga, Armand Duplantis, vigente campeón de este galardón, se encuentra de nuevo entre los nominados. 'Mondo' batió su propio récord del mundo en marzo, con 6,31 metros, y se proclamó campeón del mundo en pista cubierta, además de campeón europeo y del Ultimate. Completan la nómina de candidatos a atleta del año los estadounidenses Kenneth Bednarek y Ja'Kobe Tharp, el esloveno Kristjan Ceh, el italiano Andy Díaz, el brasileño Alison Dos Santos, el botsuano Collen Kebinatshipi, el británico Josh Kerr, el esrilanqués Rumesh Tharanga Pathirage y el keniano Sabastian Sawe.

articles.title: India, Qatar among seven bidders as race to host 2036 Olympics takes shape
articles.summary: India's ambition to host the 2036 Olympics has taken another major step forward, with the International Olympic Committee (IOC) on Tuesday confirming the
articles.body: India's ambition to host the 2036 Olympics has taken another major step forward, with the International Olympic Committee (IOC) on Tuesday confirming the country among seven bidders in the race to stage the Summer Games. Qatar, South Korea, Germany, Hungary, Turkey and South Africa are the other countries currently in discussions with the IOC, setting up what could become one of the most competitive Olympic hosting contests in years.The IOC is aiming to select the 2036 host in 2029 through a vote of its 100-plus members. The timeline represents a return to a more traditional contested process after the fast-track and largely closed-door approach used to award the 2032 Games to Brisbane. The IOC has also kept the possibility of discussions extending towards the 2040 and 2044 editions.Ahmedabad at centre of India's Olympic ambitionIndia's proposal is centred on Ahmedabad, which is scheduled to host the 2030 Commonwealth Games and boasts the Narendra Modi Stadium, the world's largest cricket stadium. India has been openly pursuing the Olympics for several years, with the country's sporting administration presenting its ambitions during the Paris 2024 Games.Qatar, another prominent contender, has built substantial experience in hosting major international sporting events, including the 2022 FIFA World Cup and world championships across several Olympic sports. Its proposal is centred on Doha, although the possibility of involving other Gulf neighbours could emerge as the bid develops.A major issue for a Qatar Olympics would be the traditional July-August window. The Summer Games have been held during those months at every edition from Athens 2004 through Brisbane 2032, but Qatar's extreme summer temperatures could require a change to the established calendar.Seven bids, with more time for competitionSouth Korea's proposal would be anchored by Seoul, which hosted the 1988 Olympics, while events could be spread across the country. Germany's bid is centred on Munich, which previously hosted the Summer Games in 1972. South Africa is proposing a national bid centred on Cape Town and is seeking to deliver the first African-hosted Summer Olympics of the modern era.Hungary and Turkey have put forward Budapest and Istanbul respectively as their proposed host cities. The IOC has set October 31 as the deadline for other national Olympic committees to express an interest in entering the 2036 race. It has also published a 30-page document outlining the framework and requirements for prospective bidders.The next major milestone will come in March, when the IOC executive board, chaired by president Kirsty Coventry, is expected to approve a shortlist of candidates that will proceed to develop detailed hosting projects.IOC promises wider choice before 2029 voteCoventry, a two-time Olympic swimming champion, has changed the approach to selecting future hosts since taking over as IOC president in June 2025. Her first major decision was to pause the previous fast-track process, giving IOC members a greater say in choosing the host.IOC members had expressed a desire for a genuine choice between multiple candidates rather than simply endorsing a preferred option put forward by the executive board. The eventual vote is now targeted for 2029, giving the shortlisted bidders roughly two and a half years to develop and promote their proposals.“Wherever the Games take place, one thing must never change: Athletes have to be at the heart of everything we do,” Coventry said.The IOC's membership includes sports administrators, current and former athletes, members of royal families, politicians, business leaders and personalities such as Oscar-winning actress Michelle Yeoh. Among those eligible to participate in the eventual vote are India's Nita Ambani and Qatar's Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani, adding another layer of interest to a contest that could ultimately stretch beyond the 2036 Games.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Los Juegos de 2036 ya tienen siete candidatas: India, Alemania, Qatar...
articles.standfirst: El COI oficializa los pasos a seguir por las sedes que optan a albergar la cita olímpica que tomará el testigo de Brisbane
articles.summary: El COI oficializa los pasos a seguir por las sedes que optan a albergar la cita olímpica que tomará el testigo de Brisbane
articles.body: El Comité Olímpico Internacional los pasos que se van a seguir para elegir la sede de los Juegos de 2036 mediante la publicación de un manual para los posibles anfitriones que deseen optar a organizar esta cita olímpica. El COI reconoce que ha mantenido un diálogo continuo con varios Comités Olímpicos Nacionales (CON) que llevan meses o incluso años trabajando en la planificación de dichos Juegos. Alemania, Hungría, India, Qatar, Corea del Sur, Sudáfrica y Turquía son los países que están ahora misma en la carrera para ser anfitriones olímpicos. Han sido invitados a presentar sus proyectos a la Comisión de Selección de la Futura Sede en noviembre. En marzo de 2027, el Consejo Ejecutivo del COI preseleccionará a las ciudades interesadas para que avancen con sus proyectos. En diciembre de 2028, habrá un nuevo proceso de selección en el que las ciudades que siguen en liza entablarán un diálogo específico con el COI cuyos miembros elegirán la sede a mediados de 2029. Las candidaturas serán evaluadas en función de una serie de factores técnicos como un plan maestro del recinto y experiencia del deportista; estrategia de financiación; apoyo político y público; capacidades de distribución de los Juegos y estrategia de legado para crear beneficios a largo plazo para las comunidades anfitrionas. "Dondequiera que se celebren los Juegos, una cosa nunca debe cambiar: los deportistas deben ser el centro de todo lo que hacemos. Como deportista, pasas años trabajando para hacer realidad tu sueño olímpico. La experiencia que vives cuando finalmente llegas a los Juegos Olímpicos te acompaña el resto de tu vida. Por eso, para cada futura sede, brindar la mejor experiencia posible a los deportistas debe ser siempre el punto de partida", afirmó Kirsty Coventry, presidenta del COI. Múnich es la apuesta de Alemania para los Juegos, bien sea en 2036, 2040 o 2044, según anunció la Confederación Alemana de Deportes Olímpicos (DOSB). La capital de Baviera, que ya acogió unos Juegos Olímpicos en 1972, venció en la votación final la candidatura de la región de Colonia-Rin-Ruhr. Berlín, también candidata en principio, acabó retirándose de la carrera. India se decanta por la ciudad de Ahmedabad, en el estado occidental de Gujarat, como la favorita por la enorme inversión en infraestructura deportiva que está recibiendo en los últimos años. La India, el país más poblado del mundo según las estimaciones de la ONU, podría convertirse en el cuarto país asiático en albergar unos Juegos Olímpicos de Verano tras Japón (Tokio 1964 y 2020), Corea del Sur (Seúl 1988) y China (Pekín 2008). Los 22 países miembros de la Liga Árabe respaldaron la candidatura de Qatar para albergar los Juegos Olímpicos y Paralímpicos de 2036. De ser elegida Doha, su capital, se convertiría en la primera de la historia en celebrarse en Oriente Medio. A finales de 2025, el Gobierno de Sudáfrica ya anunció oficialmente su intención de presentar una candidatura. Ciudad del Cabo, capital legislativa de Sudáfrica, ya había presentado una candidatura para organizar los Juegos Olímpicos de 2004, que finalmente se adjudicaron a Atenas en una votación celebrada en 1997. Durban y Johannesburgo también están entre las opciones que maneja Sudáfrica. Hungría se postula con Budapest como estandarte y Turquía con Estambul. Corea del Sur aspira a repetir tras su experiencia de 1988 con una posible candidatura conjunta entre Seúl y Jeonbuk. Esta última ciudad se había impuesto hace un año a la capital surcoreana como la elegida para optar a los Juegos de 2036. Jeonbuk reconoció ciertas limitaciones, como la falta de alojamiento y estadios que limitarían sus opciones. Ante este escenario puso sobre la mesa la opción de un plan de organización conjunta con Seúl que todavía se está negociando.

articles.title: Qatar and India among seven countries bidding for 2036 Olympics, IOC says
articles.summary: South Africa, Turkiye, Germany, Hungary and South Korea are on the list of countries revealed by the IOC.
articles.body:
Qatar’s bid to host the 2036 Summer Olympics has been confirmed by the International Olympic Committee (IOC), which said India was also among the seven countries in the running.

South Africa, Germany, Hungary, Turkiye and South Korea make up the rest of the current list issued by the IOC on Tuesday.

Other countries have until October 31 to declare an interest.

Qatar hosted the 2022 football World Cup and was home to the 2006 Asian Games, which it will host again in 2030.

In March 2027, the IOC Executive Board will draw up a shortlist of the interested parties, who will then enter dialogue with the Olympic body.

The IOC said the 2036 hosts would be assessed on factors such as funding and political and public support.

“Wherever the Games take place, one thing must never change: Athletes have to be at the heart of everything we do,” IOC President Kirsty Coventry said in a statement.

“That is why, for every future host, delivering the best possible experience for the athletes must always be the starting point,” the Zimbabwean former swimmer added.

India has stated its intention to host an Olympics for the first time, centred on Ahmedabad, the key city in Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s home state of Gujarat.

Ahmedabad will host the 2030 multisport Commonwealth Games, seen as a major rehearsal for an Olympics. The city is also home to the world’s largest cricket stadium.

South Africa hosted the 2010 football World Cup and the 1995 Rugby World Cup but has never played host to an Olympics.

An Olympics in the Gulf would have to be moved to later than its traditional July-August slot due to the heat.

The German National Olympic Committee voted last month to select Munich as its candidate city for a Games that will take place a century after the infamous 1936 Berlin Olympics, which were overseen by the Nazi regime.

The Turkish Olympic authorities hope to do one better than in the bidding for the 2020 Summer Olympics, when Istanbul came second to Tokyo.

The 2028 Summer Olympics will take place in Los Angeles, while Brisbane has been awarded the 2032 edition.

Preferred hosts ⁠⁠will be named in ⁠⁠2028, and a final decision is expected in mid-2029, the IOC said.

articles.title: 2036 Olympic Games: South Africa hope to host first African event as seven countries express interest
articles.summary: The International Olympic Committee confirms South Africa have shown an interest in becoming the first African host of the summer Olympics.
articles.body:
The International Olympic Committee (IOC) has confirmed South Africa have shown an interest in becoming the first African host of the summer Olympics in 2036.

Hungary, India, Qatar and Turkey are also working towards becoming first-time hosts, while Germany and South Korea are in discussions with the IOC having held previous summer Games.

The IOC stated that the seven countries are engaged in "continuous dialogue" with the governing body and have set a deadline of 31 October for submissions of stated interest.

Virtual presentations will be given by interested parties to the body's future host commission in November, with IOC feasibility assessments to be carried out by March 2027.

After that, the national Olympic committees, all of whom have previously announced an intention to explore hosting bids, will enter strategic dialogue with the IOC.

The South Africa proposal involves hosting between three cities - Cape Town, Durban and Johannesburg.

Durban had been set to host the Commonwealth Games in 2022, but withdrew in 2017 .

Ahmedabad, which will welcome the Commonwealth Games in 2030 and has bid for the 2038 Asian Games, will be the host city in India's bid.

The city has also staged four of the last five finals in cricket's Indian Premier League at its Narendra Modi stadium, which is reported to have a capacity of 132,000 and is named after the current prime minister of India, who hails from the city.

Budapest and Doha, the capital cities of Hungary and Qatar respectively, are the hosts in their country's bids.

Qatar hosted football's 2022 World Cup, with multiple stadia in the capital, while Budapest has staged the 2022 World Aquatics Championships and 2023 World Athletics Championships.

Istanbul is the nominated city in Turkey's bid, having previously bid unsuccessfully for the 2000, 2008 and 2020 Games.

The largest city in Turkey will host the 2027 European Games.

Germany has hosted the Olympics in 1936 and 1972, in Berlin and Munich respectively, while the latter city is bidding again for 2036.

Meanwhile South Korea capital Seoul, which hosted the Games in 1988, is part of a bid that also involves the province of North Jeolla.

The IOC also confirmed that a number of national Olympic committees are taking part in non-committal talks with the IOC about hosting future Olympic Games beyond 2036.

The UK government said in May that it is in "discussions about supporting potential bids" for the Olympics and Paralympics in the 2040s.

The 2028 Games will be held in Los Angeles, while Australia will host the Olympics for the first time in 32 years when Brisbane stages the event in 2032.

articles.title: KOPIE - IOC: India and Qatar among seven countries bidding for 2036 Olympics
articles.summary: India and Qatar are among seven countries interested in hosting the 2036 Olympics, the International Olympic Committee (IOC) said on Tuesday. An IOC statemen...
articles.body:
India and Qatar are among seven countries interested in hosting the 2036 Olympics, the International Olympic Committee (IOC) said on Tuesday.

An IOC statement said that Germany, Hungary, South Africa, South Korea and Turkey were the other interested parties before an October 31 deadline.

Germany and South Korea are the only two of the seven countries to have hosted Olympic Games in the past.

"We are looking forward to the international competition and are entering the next phase with a great deal of confidence. We have very good arguments to ultimately prevail internationally as well," Munich's Mayor Dominik Krause told dpa.

The IOC said that the seven will make presentations to the IOC's Future Host Commission in November as part of a continuous dialogue which after an IOC feasibility assessment will be followed by a strategic dialogue of candidates with the IOC executive board chaired by president Kirsty Coventry from March 2027 onwards.

A select number of preferred hosts is to be chosen for a targeted dialogue by the IOC in November 2028, with the host to be elected by all IOC members at its session in 2029.

"Wherever the Games take place, one thing must never change: athletes have to be at the heart of everything we do," swimming gold medallist Coventry said.

"As an athlete, you spend years working to make your Olympic dream come true. The experience you have when you finally reach the Olympic Games stays with you for the rest of your life.

"That is why, for every future host, delivering the best possible experience for the athletes must always be the starting point."

Qatar was long been considered a strong candidate and has staged world championships in major Olympic sports but the Iran war showed that it could be a risky choice.

Should it be awarded the Games, they would have to take place outside the traditional July/August slot because of the intense heat, like it happened when the country hosted the 2022 football World Cup.

India has also been touted as a future host, but there are concerns around its bid centring on the city of Ahmedabad, ranging from infrastructure and pollution to a weak standing on the Olympic sporting stage.

Germany is bidding with the 1972 hosts Munich who will continue for 2040 or 2044 if not successful for 2036. The 2036 Games are 100 years after those in Berlin held during the Nazi era.

Istanbul has made several unsuccessful attempts for Turkey and aims to impress by hosting next year's European Games. Hungary has also been interested for years with Budapest, but a planned bid in the past collapsed in 2017.

Olympic Games have meanwhile never taken place on the African continent but Senegal's Dakar will host the Youth Olympics later this year. South Africa is planning a joint effort from Johannesburg, Cape Town and Durban.

South Korea's bid with the Jeonbuk region is said to be controversial and plans to team up with 1988 hosts Seoul have reportedly drawn concern in the capital. There are also signals that a bid could be dropped if there is no adequate preparation time.

The 2028 Games are in Los Angeles and the 2032 edition in Brisbane.
